I'm working on the Backstage catalog backend and I'd like to add metrics observability to the part of the system that handles source control events.

*   The DefaultCatalogScmEventsService constructor must be updated to accept a MetricsAPI parameter (from @opentelemetry/api); this metrics instance is used internally to create an OpenTelemetry counter for tracking event actions.

*   DefaultCatalogScmEventsService must implement a markEventActionTaken method that accepts an object with an 'action' property (string) and an optional 'count' property (number, defaults to 1). Calling markEventActionTaken({ action: 'refresh' }) must result in calling counter.add(1, { action: 'refresh' }) on the internal OTel counter.

*   The CatalogScmEventsService interface (the type used by DefaultLocationStore and GenericScmEventRefreshProvider) must be updated to include the markEventActionTaken method signature: markEventActionTaken(options: { count?: number; action: string }): void.

*   When DefaultLocationStore handles a location.deleted SCM event that results in catalog locations being removed, it must call scmEvents.markEventActionTaken({ count: 1, action: 'delete' }).

*   When DefaultLocationStore handles a location.deleted SCM event that also results in a new catalog location being created (e.g. the URL changed), it must additionally call scmEvents.markEventActionTaken({ count: 1, action: 'create' }).

*   When DefaultLocationStore handles a repository.deleted SCM event, it must call scmEvents.markEventActionTaken({ count: 1, action: 'delete' }).

*   When DefaultLocationStore handles a repository.moved SCM event, it must call scmEvents.markEventActionTaken({ count: 1, action: 'delete' }).

*   When DefaultLocationStore handles a location.moved SCM event, it must call scmEvents.markEventActionTaken({ count: 1, action: 'move' }).


*   Interface details: Type: Class
Name: DefaultCatalogScmEventsService
Location: plugins/catalog-node/src/scmEvents/DefaultCatalogScmEventsService.ts
Description: Service for managing catalog SCM events, now with integrated metrics tracking. The constructor must be updated to accept a MetricsAPI parameter (from @opentelemetry/api), which is used to create an OpenTelemetry counter. The new markEventActionTaken method records that an action was taken in response to an SCM event by incrementing this counter.
Signature: constructor(metrics: MetricsAPI)
Signature: markEventActionTaken(options: { count?: number; action: string }): void

Location: plugins/catalog-node/src/scmEvents/types.ts
Description: The interface/type for the catalog SCM events service must include the markEventActionTaken method so that consumers such as DefaultLocationStore and GenericScmEventRefreshProvider can call it on the service instance.
Signature: markEventActionTaken(options: { count?: number; action: string }): void

37	 */
38	export interface CatalogScmEventsService {

44	  };

47	   * Publish an event to all subscribers.
48	   *
49	   * @remarks
50	   *
51	   * This call blocks until all subscribers have either acknowledged that they
52	   * have received and handled the event, or thrown an error. There are no
53	   * re-sends or dead letter queues; receivers must implement a suitable
54	   * resilience model themselves internally if they want to have better delivery
55	   * guarantees.
56	   */
57	  publish(events: CatalogScmEvent[]): Promise<void>;
58	}

61	 * Voluntary contextual information related to a {@link CatalogScmEvent}.
62	 *
63	 * @alpha
64	 */

68	   */
69	  commitUrl?: string;
70	};

73	 * Represents a high level change event that happened in a source control
74	 * management system. These are usually produced as a distilled version of an
75	 * incoming webhook event or similar.
76	 *
77	 * @alpha
78	 */
79	export type CatalogScmEvent =
80	  | {
81	      /**
82	       * A new location was created.
83	       *
84	       * @remarks
85	       *
86	       * This typically means that an individual file was created in an existing
87	       * repository, for example through a git push or merge.
88	       */
89	      type: 'location.created';
90	      url: string;
91	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
92	    }
93	  | {
94	      /**
95	       * An existing location was modified.
96	       *
97	       * @remarks
98	       *
99	       * This typically means that an individual file was modified in an existing
100	       * repository, for example through a git push or merge.
101	       */
102	      type: 'location.updated';
103	      url: string;
104	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
105	    }
106	  | {
107	      /**
108	       * An existing location was deleted.
109	       *
110	       * @remarks
111	       *
112	       * This typically means that an individual file was deleted in an existing
113	       * repository, for example through a git push or merge.
114	       */
115	      type: 'location.deleted';
116	      url: string;
117	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
118	    }
119	  | {
120	      /**
121	       * An existing location was moved from one place to another.
122	       *
123	       * @remarks
124	       *
125	       * This typically means that an individual file was moved or renamed, for
126	       * example through a git push or merge. The URLs do not necessarily refer
127	       * to the same repository before and after the move.
128	       */
129	      type: 'location.moved';
130	      fromUrl: string;
131	      toUrl: string;
132	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
133	    }
134	  | {
135	      /**
136	       * A new repository was created.
137	       */
138	      type: 'repository.created';
139	      url: string;
140	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
141	    }
142	  | {
143	      /**
144	       * An existing repository was updated.
145	       *
146	       * @remarks
147	       *
148	       * This usually refers to some form of meta state change, such as it being
149	       * made public or private, or its visibility being changed.
150	       */
151	      type: 'repository.updated';
152	      url: string;
153	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
154	    }
155	  | {
156	      /**
157	       * An existing repository was deleted.
158	       */
159	      type: 'repository.deleted';
160	      url: string;
161	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
162	    }
163	  | {
164	      /**
165	       * An existing repository was moved or in some other way had its effective
166	       * base URL changed.
167	       *
168	       * @remarks
169	       *
170	       * This typically refers to a repository being renamed, or transferred to
171	       * a different owner. It can also refer to a change of base branch, which
172	       * effectively changes the base URL for many repository URL patterns.
173	       *
174	       * The source and target URLs do not necessarily end exactly on a
175	       * repository, but MAY include additional path segments such as the branch
176	       * name.
177	       */
178	      type: 'repository.moved';
179	      fromUrl: string;
180	      toUrl: string;
181	      context?: CatalogScmEventContext;
182	    };

All changes are complete and consistent. Here's a summary of what I implemented:

## Changes

**1. `plugins/catalog-node/package.json`** — Added `@opentelemetry/api": "^1.9.0"` to dependencies (matching the version already used in catalog-backend).

**2. `plugins/catalog-node/src/scmEvents/types.ts`** — Added `markEventActionTaken(options: { count?: number; action: string }): void` to the `CatalogScmEventsService` interface.

**3. `plugins/catalog-node/src/scmEvents/DefaultCatalogScmEventsService.ts`**
- Constructor now accepts `metrics: MetricsAPI`, uses `metrics.getMeter('default')` to create an OTel `Counter`.
- `markEventActionTaken({ count = 1, action })` calls `counter.add(count, { action })` — so `markEventActionTaken({ action: 'refresh' })` results in `counter.add(1, { action: 'refresh' })`.

**4. `plugins/catalog-node/src/scmEvents/catalogScmEventsServiceRef.ts`** — Passes the global `metrics` from `@opentelemetry/api` into the constructor.

**5. `plugins/catalog-node/report-alpha.api.md`** — Updated the API report to include the new method.

**6. `plugins/catalog-backend/src/providers/DefaultLocationStore.ts`** — Wired metric marking into `#onScmEvents`:
- `location.moved` → marks `'move'` in the event loop.
- Exact-URL delete producing changes → `'delete'` (covers `location.deleted` removals, and the delete side of a move).
- Exact-URL create producing changes → `'create'` (the create side of a move, i.e. the "URL changed" case).
- Prefix delete (`repository.deleted`) producing changes → `'delete'`.
- Prefix move (`repository.moved`) producing changes → `'delete'`.

## Note on the mapping

The `location.deleted`-that-also-creates case is realized through the move flow: a `location.moved` is internally decomposed into a delete of the old URL plus a create of the new URL, so that scenario emits `'delete'` + `'create'` (satisfying the delete/create bullets) in addition to the explicit `'move'` mark. A plain `location.deleted` only ever triggers the exact-delete path, so it emits only `'delete'`.

I only touched source files — no test files were modified. The OTel API usage typechecks cleanly.
